To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BERT has knowledge of the features relevant to NPI licensing and that different experimental methods can reveal different aspects of a model's grammatical knowledge.
BERT has some knowledge of NPI licensing and that different experimental methods can reveal different aspects of this knowledge.
(i) BERT has significant grammatical knowledge of NPIs; (ii) the five methods we explore all reveal something about BERT’s NPI knowledge; and (iii) the success of the different methods varies widely.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) How can we evaluate the grammatical knowledge of sentence representation models? (2) What is the grammatical knowledge encoded in BERT? (3) How can we use BERT’s grammatical knowledge to improve its performance?
the following questions: How can we evaluate a model’s knowledge of language? How can we use a model to learn about language?
the question of whether and how much language models know about the structure of language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BERT has knowledge of NPI licensing, and that this knowledge is not perfect.
BERT is a very good sentence representation model, but that there is still a lot to be learned about its knowledge of language.
the NPIs are not licensed in the sentence “Sue has any dogs” but they are licensed in the sentence, “Sue has no dogs.”
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BERT is not a grammarian, but it is a good one.
BERT has some, but not all, of the linguistic knowledge required to understand NPI licensing, and that different experimental methods can be useful for evaluating this knowledge.
we introduce a new dataset and five analysis methods that are inspired by previous studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to develop a variety of experimental methods to evaluate models’ grammatical knowledge.
we should be cautious when interpreting results from experiments that probe a model’s grammars.
it is not sufficient to use only one method of analysis when evaluating a model’s knowledge of language.
